Unit tests prove every rocking vertex (cup, lid, tamper ring) stays inside the standard slot and at least 5 mm from the gizmo arcs, arrowheads and gimbal ring over the full 9 s cycle and the still pose
deviations: Euler gizmo radius 0.20 instead of 0.16: from the gizmo center (0, 0.24, 0) the rocking lid edge sweeps 0.15 to 0.18 m and the gimbal ring is at 0.153 m, so 0.16 m arcs would pass through the lid. Center, tube, quarter arcs, one per axis and arrowheads are as specified.
Gimbal mechanics: the ring pitches on the outer pins at +-X (as specified) and the cup rolls on two added inner pins at +-Z, so every join is real and nothing floats while it rocks.

Whole object turned -30 degrees about Y (OBJECT_YAW) for a three-quarter view: square on, the pitch and yaw arcs and the pin axes are edge-on to the stop camera (the pitch arc read as a stub on the lid). The cut-away wedge is turned back so it faces the camera exactly.

Lid split into a full-circle floor (print layers 0 and 1) and the 270 degree cover (layers 2 to 9) with a pocket, so the board rests on the floor inside the wedge; the cover's cut faces are closed with the stepped section. The tamper ring is a 270 degree arc cut like the cover, since a full ring would span the open wedge in mid-air.

When runtime.motion turns false (idle stop, reduced motion, low tier) the object eases over 1 s to the still pose instead of freezing mid-cycle; it mounts directly in the pose when motion is off, so ?test=1 is identical from the first frame.
